correction.description: Generalize active correction #5's sibling-appropriations disambiguation so it catches UniqueKey collisions among <appropriations>-derived Division rows regardless of their structural sibling status or `level` attribute. Two viable approaches: (a) incorporate the <appropriations> `level` attribute (major / intermediate / small) into the heading-derived UniqueKey position so a small-level 'contingent expenses of the senate' never collides with an intermediate-level 'Contingent Expenses of the Senate' even after case-folding; or (b) extend the post-pass _disambiguate_sibling_appropriations so it triggers on ANY two Division rows within the same pLaw that end up sharing a UniqueKey (not only direct same-parent siblings), appending sequential ordinals in OriginalOrder to the deepest non-null DivisionHeadingLevel. For PL 92-18 in vol 85 the two affected rows are OriginalOrder 152 (intermediate-level 'Contingent Expenses of the Senate' under LEGISLATIVE BRANCH; Text=Senate policy committees / Automobiles / Inquiries / Folding documents / Miscellaneous items) and OriginalOrder 157 (small-level 'contingent expenses of the senate' appearing as a sibling of intermediate 'Joint Items' under LEGISLATIVE BRANCH; Text=Joint Economic Committee / Joint Committee on Atomic Energy / Joint Committee on Printing). Approach (a) is preferred because it preserves DivisionHeadingLevel2 unchanged and incorporates a real structural signal already present in the XML.

When a pLaw contains both (a) one or more <section> elements lacking a parseable <num value=...> attribute and (b) one or more <section> elements whose parsed SectionNumber starts at 1, the null-fallback ordinal for the unnumbered section(s) must be assigned starting after the maximum parsed SectionNumber present in the same pLaw (or, equivalently, use a distinct slot — e.g. ordinal 0 or a prefixed namespace — so the unnumbered intro 'That—' section does not collapse onto parsed Section 1). For PL 91-185 specifically: the unnumbered 'That—' intro section currently gets SectionNumber-position '1', which collides with the real Section 1 that follows. Ordering should preserve document order (OriginalOrder).
